title: Markowitz (1952) Portfolio Selection

methods.name: mean_variance_optimization
methods.extraction: Diversification benefit derived from covariance; portfolio variance is not a weighted average of variances. Efficient frontier where return is maximised per unit of variance.

title: Fama & French (1992) Cross-Section of Expected Stock Returns

methods.name: size_and_book_to_market_factor_construction
methods.extraction: Sort universe by size (market cap) and B/M; long-short portfolios capture cross-sectional risk premia not explained by CAPM.

title: Fama & French (1993) Common risk factors

methods.name: three_factor_regression
methods.extraction: Market, SMB, HML factor portfolios; time-series regression of asset returns on factor returns yields exposures (betas).

title: Fama & French (2015) Five-factor model

methods.name: five_factor_regression
methods.extraction: Adds profitability (RMW) and investment (CMA) factors. Reduces HML to redundant in their original test universe.

title: Carhart (1997) On Persistence in Mutual Fund Performance

methods.name: momentum_factor_construction
methods.extraction: Cross-sectional 12-2 month past-return ranking long-short portfolio captures momentum premium not explained by FF3.

title: Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) Momentum

methods.name: cross_sectional_momentum
methods.extraction: 3-12 month formation periods, 1-12 month holding periods; J-month winners outperform losers in 6-12 month holding window.

title: Asness, Moskowitz, Pedersen (2013) Value and Momentum Everywhere

methods.name: cross_asset_value_and_momentum
methods.extraction: Value and momentum coexist across equities, bonds, currencies, commodities; negatively correlated with each other.

title: Asness, Frazzini, Pedersen (2019) Quality minus Junk

methods.name: quality_minus_junk_construction
methods.extraction: Quality composite (profitability + growth + safety + payout) long-short returns positive premium with low drawdowns.

title: Frazzini & Pedersen (2014) Betting Against Beta

methods.name: betting_against_beta
methods.extraction: Leverage-constrained investors crowd into high-beta stocks; low-beta stocks earn premium; BAB portfolio is leverage-neutral.

title: Sloan (1996) Accrual Anomaly

methods.name: accruals_anomaly
methods.extraction: High-accruals firms underperform low-accruals firms; mispricing of accrual quality persists into earnings announcements.

title: Bernard & Thomas (1989) PEAD

methods.name: post_earnings_announcement_drift
methods.extraction: Stocks with positive earnings surprises drift up for ~60 days post-announcement; negative surprises drift down.

title: Womack (1996) Analyst Recommendations

methods.name: analyst_recommendation_drift
methods.extraction: Stocks experience price drift after analyst upgrades / downgrades; effect concentrated in small caps.

title: Cohen, Malloy, Pomorski (2012) Insider trading

methods.name: informed_insider_trading_signal
methods.extraction: Opportunistic insiders' trades carry information; routine insiders' trades do not.

title: Boehmer, Jones, Zhang (2008) Which shorts are informed?

methods.name: informed_short_flow
methods.extraction: Short flow predicts future negative returns; effect strongest in institutional shorting.

title: Pan & Poteshman (2006) Information in option volume

methods.name: option_volume_informed_trading
methods.extraction: Put-call volume imbalance carries information about future stock returns.

title: Daniel & Moskowitz (2016) Momentum Crashes

methods.name: momentum_crash_control
methods.extraction: Momentum experiences crashes after market drawdowns; volatility-managed momentum reduces tail risk.

title: McLean & Pontiff (2016) Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?

methods.name: post_publication_factor_fading
methods.extraction: Anomaly returns are ~26-58% lower post-publication; institutional arbitrage compresses premia.

title: Harvey, Liu, Zhu (2016) And the Cross-Section of Expected Returns

methods.name: multiple_testing_threshold
methods.extraction: With 300+ published factors, naive t-stat thresholds overstate significance; recommend t>3 (Bonferroni-style) or deflated Sharpe.

title: Bailey & López de Prado (2014) Deflated Sharpe Ratio

methods.name: deflated_sharpe_ratio
methods.extraction: Adjusts observed Sharpe for backtest overfitting probability; reduces false discovery risk.

title: Frazzini, Israel, Moskowitz (2018) Trading Costs of Asset Pricing Anomalies

methods.name: real_world_trading_cost_overlay
methods.extraction: Realised slippage + commission + market impact compresses anomaly returns; capacity is far below academic gross.

title: Novy-Marx & Velikov (2016) A Taxonomy of Anomalies and Their Trading Costs

methods.name: anomaly_cost_taxonomy
methods.extraction: Anomalies vary 5x in turnover; many lose all alpha after realistic costs.

title: Cochrane (2011) Presidential Address: Discount Rates

methods.name: factor_zoo_problem
methods.extraction: Hundreds of factors published; expected return is what we don't know in cross-section.

title: Harvey Liu Zhu (2016) And the Cross-Section of Expected Returns

methods.name: factor_research_significance_threshold
methods.extraction: t>3 threshold for newly-claimed factors.

title: López de Prado & Lewis (2019) Detection of False Investment Strategies

methods.name: false_strategy_detection
methods.extraction: Probabilistic Sharpe + deflated Sharpe + backtest length controls.

title: Kahneman & Tversky (1979) Prospect Theory

methods.name: loss_aversion_in_decision_modelling
methods.extraction: Decision-makers weight losses ~2x more than gains; reference-point dependence.
methods.viza_primitive: research_only — used as cautionary framing, not direct signal

title: Daniel, Hirshleifer, Subrahmanyam (1998) Overconfidence and over-/under-reaction

methods.name: overreaction_underreaction_modelling
methods.extraction: Overconfidence -> overreaction to private info; biased self-attribution -> momentum.
